expected_features: Active floodplain, beach, spit and estuarine forms
Mapped by geomorphology, not by rock exposure
engineering_note: Unconsolidated, saturated and mobile: low strength, high settlement, and shifting channels and shorelines make it poor founding ground and prone to scour and erosion.
mineral_note: Principal host of Ghana's alluvial gold and diamond placers (e.g. Birim River) and the main source of construction sand and gravel.

expected_features: Soft, poorly lithified bouldery shale and pebbly grit
engineering_note: Very soft and easily excavated, but the lateritic clays shrink, swell and erode readily; low bearing capacity and poor slope stability where saturated.

expected_features: Thin fossiliferous marine limestone and glauconitic sandstone
Gentle (2-6 degree) seaward dips, largely soil and swamp covered
engineering_note: Poorly consolidated, water-saturated coastal sands and clays: soft, compressible ground with a shallow water table, so expect settlement and excavation-support issues.
mineral_note: Ghana's key petroleum system: organic-rich shales and porous sands act as source and reservoir for offshore and onshore oil and gas (e.g. Jubilee Field, Tano Basin).

expected_features: Granitoid dropstones in dark Ajua Shale
Siderite nodules and pyrite in upper shales
Coastal fault-block exposures (Dixcove to Cape Coast)
engineering_note: Interbedded sandstone, shale and conglomerate of very uneven strength; block-faulted and coastal, so cliff stability and rapid facies changes matter for any works.
mineral_note: No significant ore; notable for classic, accessible unconformity exposures along Western Region coastal cliffs.

expected_features: Very mature (near-pure quartz) arenites and grits
Gentle dips; central Accra coastal exposures
engineering_note: Mature quartz arenites are hard and stable; the fine grey shale and mudstone interbeds are the weak layer to watch on cuts and foundations.
Generally flat-lying and stable; watch for mudstone interbeds.
mineral_note: Limited metallic potential; some industrial sand and clay.

expected_features: Basal glacial triad: tillite, cap carbonate, cherty silixite
Greenish-grey thinly bedded shale and wacke (flysch)
Varves, microfolds and calcite veining in limestones
Greenish-grey Oti beds grading up into red Obosum beds
engineering_note: Shale-dominated and generally weak, with soft mudstone interbeds; limestone bands are firmer but may be karstic, so check for solution features.
mineral_note: Oti limestones (Bimbila, Buipe) are evaluated for cement; minor barite in the cap carbonates, and bitumen seeps drive current hydrocarbon exploration.

expected_features: Large-scale cross-bedding, ripple marks, flute casts
Thin basal conglomerate over the basement unconformity
engineering_note: Well-cemented quartz arenite is strong and stable, forming steep escarpments; it is a productive fractured-rock aquifer, so expect water in joints and fractures.
mineral_note: No metallic ores; regionally important as a fractured-rock aquifer and as an escarpment-forming building-stone source.

expected_features: Volcanic breccia, agglomerate and tuff interbeds
engineering_note: Fresh mafic lavas are hard and resistant (ridge-forming); serpentinised ultramafic pods along thrust planes can be weak and slippery, so watch the contacts.
Mixed strengths: hard chert, jasper and sandstone bands set against weak, tectonically foliated shales; expect variable competence and structurally controlled weakness along thrusts.
mineral_note: Minor ornamental jasper ('tiger eye') and limited hematite iron occurrences; not a major ore host.

engineering_note: Quartzites are hard and competent (good aggregate and dimension stone), but interbedded phyllites and schists are weak and fissile; bedding-parallel failure and anisotropy are the concern on slopes and cuts.
mineral_note: No significant metallic mineralization; flaggy quartzites are worked locally for dimension stone and aggregate.

engineering_note: Competent quartzitic units; good foundation but abrasive to drill.
mineral_note: Paleoplacer gold in the Banket conglomerate reefs.

engineering_note: Fresh rock is strong; weathered cap can be 20-40 m of saprolite.
mineral_note: Primary host of Ashanti-style gold; also Cu and minor base metals.

engineering_note: Deeply weathered profile with variable rockhead depth; probe before founding.
mineral_note: Hosts orogenic gold in shear zones and quartz veins.

engineering_note: Quartzo-feldspathic gneiss forming low-relief flat ground (Accra Plains); fresh rock is firm, but weathering depth is variable, so verify rockhead locally.
Dense, hard, high-strength rock widely quarried for construction aggregate; forms steep inselbergs, so slope stability matters on and around outcrops.
mineral_note: No metallic ores of note; valued as high-strength crushed-rock aggregate. Inselbergs carry cultural and geoheritage significance.

engineering_note: Fresh granitoid is strong and competent, but deep tropical weathering commonly leaves thick sandy-clay saprolite over a hard lateritic cap; probe for true rockhead before founding.
mineral_note: Not a primary ore host itself, but its shear corridors help control mesothermal gold; local pegmatites carry kaolin (e.g. Saltpond).
